itens.titulo: Stock Market Today, Oct. 14: Bank of America Shares Fall 5% on Earnings Miss and Compliance Penalty
itens.descricao: Stock Market Today, Oct. 14: Bank of America Shares Fall 5% on Earnings Miss and Compliance Penalty Yahoo Finance
trechos: Bank of America (NYSE:BAC), a global consumer, commercial, and investment banking franchise, closed at $51.39, down 4.76%.
Trading volume reached 115.1M shares, coming in about 226% above its three-month average of 35.3M shares.
How the markets moved today S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,721, down 1.08%, and Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) closed at 26,693, down 1.88%.

Among diversified banks and financial services peers, JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) closed at $335.28, up 1.16%, while Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) closed at $80.91, up 0.20%, highlighting a mixed day for large-bank shares.
What this means for investors Bank of America briefly suffered its biggest single-day drop since April 2025 after missing Q3 earnings and being hit with a $1.2 billion fine from the U.S.
The fine amounted to a $0.17 hit to EPS in Q3, but even without including this figure, BAC stock's EPS of $1.08 came up two cents short of what Wall Street was expecting.
After being down nearly 10% early in the morning, Bank of America recovered roughly 5% throughout the day.
While the fine certainly sticks out, it was mostly a "fine" quarter for BofA, so investors shouldn't overreact one way or the other.

itens.titulo: Alibaba Stock Is Down 38% From Its 2025 High. JPMorgan Sees 81% Upside
itens.descricao: Alibaba Stock Is Down 38% From Its 2025 High. JPMorgan Sees 81% Upside Yahoo Finance
trechos: Key Takeaways - JPMorgan lowered its Alibaba price target from $210 to $200 while maintaining its Overweight rating, implying approximately 81% upside from the October 12 share price.
- Alibaba stock closed roughly 38% below its October 2025 high as weaker earnings and substantial investments weighed on investor sentiment.
- Alibaba's cloud revenue grew 45% in the June quarter, while analysts anticipate a significant earnings recovery through fiscal 2028.
- JPMorgan's $200 target is possible, but it requires a meaningful earnings recovery.
Alibaba's current valuation offers a more compelling case than assuming the stock will reach $200.
Alibaba Group Holding (BABA) has fallen sharply from its 2025 highs, but JPMorgan still sees substantial upside for the Chinese technology giant.
On October 12, JPMorgan analyst Alex Yao lowered his Alibaba price target from $210 to $200 while maintaining an Overweight rating.
Based on the stock's price of approximately $110.80 at the time, the revised target implied roughly 81% upside.

itens.titulo: O Bradesco saiu de moda na bolsa? O rali eleitoral tem seus queridinhos — e BBDC4 ficou de escanteio
itens.descricao: O Bradesco saiu de moda na bolsa? O rali eleitoral tem seus queridinhos — e BBDC4 ficou de escanteio Seu Dinheiro
trechos: O rali eleitoral tem seus queridinhos — e BBDC4 ficou de escanteio A disparada das ações financeiras não beneficiou todos da mesma forma.
O desempenho de Flávio Bolsonaro nas eleições, com o segundo turno marcado para 25 de outubro, ajudou a alimentar as apostas em uma agenda econômica mais favorável ao mercado.
Na semana, o Ibovespa avançou 14% em dólares, enquanto o setor financeiro acumulou alta de 22%.
Os bancos digitais dispararam 37%, seguidos pelas empresas de mercado de capitais, com valorização de 36%, e pelas companhias de pagamentos, que subiram 27%.
Na outra ponta, os bancos tradicionais avançaram 15%, enquanto as seguradoras tiveram o desempenho mais modesto, com alta de 8%.

Leia Também O que os investidores esperam do 2º turno das eleições Para os mais otimistas, uma eventual vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro abriria espaço para reformas econômicas, juros mais baixos e fortalecimento do real.
Também há dúvidas sobre a duração da "lua de mel” do mercado com um eventual novo governo.
A XP (XPBR31) aparece entre os nomes mais bem cotados, à frente da B3 (B3SA3) nas preferências dos investidores consultados pelo BTG.

For the entire fiscal year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates are projecting earnings of $3.3 per share and a revenue of $49.82 billion, representing changes of +10% and +4.02%, respectively, from the prior year.

itens.titulo: 10-year Treasury yield dips as traders look ahead to Thursday economic reports
itens.descricao: 10-year Treasury yield dips as traders look ahead to Thursday economic reports CNBC
trechos: The 10-year Treasury note yield fell on Wednesday after jumping earlier in the day as traders awaited more inflation data due out Thursday.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — slid more than 2 basis points to 5.19%.
Treasury yield — which tends to react most to geopolitical events — was down more than 4 basis points at 5.517%.
The 2-year Treasury yield — which closely tracks the Fed's interest rate decisions — gained more than 1 basis point to 4.808% after earlier hitting its highest level since Sept.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely.
The midday reversal came as equities sold off, with the S&P 500 dropping more than 1%, leading some investors to rotate back into the relative safety of the bond market.
For PPI, economists polled by Dow Jones are expecting a 0.6% rise on the month and a 5.5% gain on the year.
The data will follow Wednesday's September consumer price index report, which rose 3.7% year over year, higher than the Dow Jones consensus estimate of 3.6%.
